sara_pm: Morning — Search relevance launch went out. We have ~20 bug reports + 16 enhancement requests flagged by CS. Need to decide how to split next sprint. Quick thoughts?

mike_eng: saw increased latency spikes on long queries. stack traces in logs look like `KVCache miss at step 2` — prioritizing bug?

nina_design: a few customers asked for highlight styling change (minor). I'd call that enhancement unless it's causing UX failure.

tara_custsucc: customer ACME says "search returns old model ranking occasionally" — severity P2. They want fix asap or rollback.

leo_data: ran eval suite; 6 regressions > 5% on our metric from canary. three correspond to specific templates (date parsing). logging attached: https://redwood.internal/wiki/qa/1831

sara_pm: Proposal: sprint split — 60% eng capacity to P0/P1 bugs (latency/regressions/ACME case), 40% for small enhancements (highlight, synonyms). Rollout criteria: 0 P0 regressions, median latency < 120ms, and automated regression tests green on canary.

mike_eng: plan: implement quick patch for `depth` caching and a nonblocking fallback in 1 day. If patch doesn't stabilise, autoscale route to older model variant.

deploy-bot: deploy v1.0.3 to canary started by sara_pm at 2026-03-19T10:15:23Z

nina_design: for highlight styling I can ship a CSS toggle flag behind a feature flag. low risk.

tara_custsucc: I'll negotiate with ACME for canary access and offer extended logs. If they accept canary, treat as P1 not P0.

leo_data: will add focused eval set for ACME templates and add to CI.

sara_pm: action items: mike -> patch + rollback plan (due EOD), leo -> eval + CI tests (tomorrow morning), nina -> feature flag UI (2 days), tara -> ACME canary negotiation (update by EOD). I'll update roadmap board and communicate scope to sales.

mike_eng: ack. Will open bug PR and tag with `postlaunch-hotfix` and `sprint-nav`.

sara_pm: decision: no rollback unless regression rate > 10% across responses. Keep enhancements in parallel but gated behind criteria. We'll reconvene 48h after canary run. :calendar:
